### Policy, holding period and what would change the answer

Deere, AGCO, CNH and Kubota have closed ag-tech deals without a public CFIUS objection; a Chinese buyer would face CFIUS review of the perception model, license and grower data, and Mexico assembly adds tariff diligence. An IPO is not realistic before 2030 at $1.9M of revenue and a $5.2M FY2025 net loss. The holding period is three to five years, 2030-2032 after a Series B. At the $90M post-money the lead gets 1.1x at $100M (1.0x after dilution), 1.7x at $150M (1.4x) and 2.8x at $250M (2.2x); over five years that is 0% IRR at $100M, 17.1% at $250M and -10.0% at the $25M bear. A 20-30% lower price or 1.5x preference would make the same exits work; at $72M the lead is buying an option that needs a $250M+ bid. The 1.04x expected return and the pass assume the deck's 1x, non-participating, equal-rank preference — one sentence on deck p.14, with no seed charter or note agreement supplied; the seed issue price is not disclosed and the $2.5M of pre-seed SAFEs may convert on top, making the stack $39.27M rather than $36.77M. The Pass therefore rests on the 1.0x floor holding at a $39.4-41.6M exit — $36.77M of stack plus debt and costs — not on a sub-1x mean. If the notes are senior or 2x the $25M recovery is 0.21x rather than 0.59x, and a $10M senior 2028 round cuts it to 0.31x; the note purchase agreement and seed charter are the open data request that would settle the downside. The implication is to pass at $72M, or invest at a 20-30% lower price with a 1.5x preference and a milestone tranche. Diligence should confirm the Advanced Farm and Tortuga prices, grower-contract ownership, the Calder license's change-of-control terms and the 53% of 2026 paid robot-seasons in two growers. [S95, S97, S93]

## ESG评估 ESG Assessment

Orrin holds no licence it can lose, but four inputs to its value case sit outside its control before 2027: a wage floor a California court reopened, a robotics tariff due by 2027-04-26, a licence test on 2027-12-31 and a California driver requirement AB 187 leaves in force. My judgement: the balance is negative for 2027 and positive after, and the inputs that decide it are conditions the company would have to meet, not risks a valuation absorbs. (S1, S126)

### The wage floor, not the robot, sets the price

The grower's alternative cost moved against Orrin in 2026. The skill-based wage floor effective 2026-08-03 puts California's entry-level adverse effect wage rate at $16.45 an hour against the $19.97 Farm Labor Survey rate that governed to 2025-10-01 — a 17.6% cut — with the experienced level at $18.71; Florida fell from $16.23 to $12.47 and $15.06. On the deck's quarter-acre per picker-day, one pass over an acre costs $526 of hand labour at Level I and $599 at Level II: $21,056–$23,949 an acre over a 40-pass season. At $9,500 a robot-season over 3.5 acres the robot is $2,714 an acre, 11%–13% of that, and $4,714 at the 2027 list price, so price is not what stops adoption: Grower B cut from 22 to 14 robots while Grower E left over bruising. On 2026-08-26 a California district court held the October 2025 methodology unlawful on four grounds — skill tiers, housing, wage survey, primary-duty rule — ordered a replacement and warned of back wages. A higher California rate is more likely than not to apply in 2027, restoring most of the 17.6% cut and lifting the ceiling [S80, S81, S1].

### The rule that stands, and who is organised

The United Farm Workers, which won that case, will shape the rule. AB 187, the session's employment trailer bill, passed both houses on 2026-08-31 and was chaptered on 2026-09-18 as Chapter 256 without the Cal/OSHA amendment that would have let unpiloted machines work beside crews; the standard requiring a human driver in agricultural workplaces therefore stands through the 2027 season, and the Standards Board's advisory committee first meets on 2026-12-01 [S126, S124, S142, S82, S115, S1]. Both readings of that rule end the investment. The mechanism is asymmetric: if a technician satisfies the standard, the 1:8 ratio is the exposure and a 1:1 technician puts field service above the season price, which means the service margin fails; if the fleet cannot satisfy it, one citation stops the only revenue line. Material restriction or enforcement in 2027: 20%–25% probability, -70% to -90% of equity value — probability times impact, not probability alone. The restriction becomes acceptable only on three conditions, none met today: a counsel opinion that a technician satisfies the human-driver standard; a Cal/OSHA interpretation or an advisory-committee outcome confirming that reading; and field service at 1:8 or better. California overtime adds to the hand cost displaced; Florida's exposure is immigration enforcement.

### The robot crosses a border being re-priced

Orrin owns the fleet, so duty lands on its capital cost. USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico enter at 0%, non-qualifying robots at 10%: $3,300 on the $33,000 v4 bill of materials, 26% of the $12,700 renewal price and 85% of a robot-season's $3,900 gross profit. The Section 232 robotics proclamation of 2026-10-28 found a threat, imposed no duty and set a Commerce–USTR update within 180 days [S88, S89]. At 25% that is $8,250 a robot, or $2.48M against a $9.9M 2027 build budget. Whether the robot meets USMCA origin is not disclosed; metals duties of 50% apply even when it does.

### A licence with a cliff, and a statute nobody has checked

The licence costs 2.5% of net robot revenue with a $40,000 minimum — the floor binds in FY2026 at 5.6% of robots-as-a-service revenue — and falls to non-exclusive below 100 robots in commercial service on 2027-12-31, against 75 paid robot-seasons and a 64-robot fleet [S1, S85, S86]. A binary test with no cure is harsher than practice, where exclusive licences carry diligence milestones and cure periods. The plan clears the threshold; the cliff needs 72% slippage (20%–25% conversion risk). If either family was federally funded, 35 U.S.C. 204 requires the exclusive US licensee to manufacture substantially in the US, and Guadalajara assembles the grippers.

### Food safety is an equipment problem now

21 CFR Part 112 names mechanical harvesters as equipment, and 112.123 requires food-contact surfaces to be smooth, cleanable and cleaned and sanitised as necessary [S83, S92]. Picking into the clamshell makes the machine's interior a packing surface, and field-packed fruit reaches the consumer unwashed. No federal certificate exists and no FDA action on machine-harvested berries was found; the gate is a retailer audit and the penalty a delisting. ISO 18497-1:2024 sets design and verification requirements for autonomous agricultural machinery, is voluntary, and no assessment against it is disclosed.

### The social case is a product metric

Labour substitution is an asset only where labour supply binds, not where quality binds: the numbers that move a purchase are the 94% pick rate, 3.8% bruising and 86% uptime, on rows excluding plastic tunnels, standing water and slopes over 4%. No retailer standard or campaign aimed at machine-harvested strawberries was identified. Governance carries more weight: Tallis is noteholder, board observer, customer, contract manufacturer and investor; the COO's own company is paid for robot moves and night supervision; the independent board seat is vacant; and ARR includes letters of intent and a contract ending 2027-06-30. USAspending returns no award under the company's name against the Phase II award the deck describes [S91, S1].

Four records are requested — the H-2A files and wage table, the SBIR award, the USPTO assignment chain and licence, and the AB 187 text — so confidence is medium on tariff and licence exposure and low on food-safety compliance. For the investor, the factors change what a season is worth, not whether Orrin can sell one; the test they set is whether the three California conditions hold before the 2027 season. (S80, S91, S85, S126)

| Issue | Why it is material | Rating impact | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| H-2A wage floor | CA $16.45 vs $19.97; FL $12.47 vs $16.23 set the hand-cost ceiling | Negative for 2027; positive if reinstated | S80 |

## 综合评分与投资建议 Comprehensive Scoring & Recommendation

Orrin scores 4.5 of 10 on the weighted evidence and the recommendation is to pass at $72M pre-money. The score is not a verdict on the picker: it is a real harvest bill — $21,056-23,949 an acre-season of hand-pick labour — and a credibly measured machine, set against a lease book that loses $8,100 a robot-season at the signed price (unverified management figures), a $33,000 build cost quoted only by a counterparty with five roles in the round, and a $90M post-money that returns the lead 1.0x until a $90M exit and 2x only at $180M. Pass rather than Wait for milestone: the binding objection is the price plus company-only evidence, and the milestones are the conditions for the lower mark, not a reason to hold these terms open. [S1, S95]

### The weighted score

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Market and customer pain | 15% | 7 | Hand-pick labour is $21,056-23,949 an acre-season and the robot fee 11-13% of it; the crop base is flat (2025 US production -1%), so growth must come from penetration, full adoption of 50,000 acres is only $236M of revenue, and the 2026 wage-floor cut lowered the grower's alternative cost by 18-23% | S80, S129, S95 |
| Product and technology | 20% | 6 | 94% pick rate on 212 company-chosen rows is a real measurement, but coverage is 1.0-1.2 acres per 24 hours against a claimed 1.5, 3.8% bruising spends 76% of the USDA allowance, and the core perception families are licensed with an exclusivity cliff at 100 robots | S1 (unverified), S86 |
| Unit economics | 20% | 2 | -$8,100 contribution per robot-season at the $9,500 signed price and $48,000 build; breakeven is $17,600 a season on that build, or a $15,600 build at the signed price; the reported 41% margin precedes $3.21M of FY2027 depreciation and -5.5% follows it, against United Rentals' 35.8-40.3% after depreciation | S1 (unverified), S132 |
| Team and execution | 10% | 5 | The founding pair fits perception and farm access and shipped three hardware generations without a CTO; nobody in the five-person executive group has built hardware at volume, the CTO seat is vacant from 2023-08, and the plan asks for 5.6x fleet growth in one season (company-reported, unverified) | S1 (unverified) |
| Competitive position | 10% | 5 | Not alone: Harvest CROO claims human-parity open-field picking (company-issued, 2025-04-24), while Advanced Farm, Tortuga and Monarch have exited or shut; the licence cliff and ungranted filings leave little enforceable exclusivity | S27, S127, S131 |
| Financial position and funding | 10% | 4 | $3.7M of cash at 2026-09-30 against $410,000 monthly burn, a $1.5M floor near 2027-03-10 if the close slips, $4.0M committed of an $18M target, and a $3.2M ARR that is 44% contracted rental, 38% related-party engineering and 19% letters (company-reported, unverified) | S1 (unverified), S95 |
| Valuation and exit | 15% | 3 | $69.9M enterprise value is 36.8x FY2025 revenue and 49.9x corrected recurring revenue against a 2.3x listed peer median; 2 of 8 ag-robotics companies have exited above $100M and none in harvesting; Blue River, the best case, was a 4x last-round outcome | S95 (unverified), S128, S127 |

Two dimensions carry the largest weight and score lowest: unit economics and valuation. The product and market scores are what make the company interesting and the price already pays for them. No dimension scores above seven without a named comparator; the market score is capped there by addressable revenue.

### What the decomposition says

Orrin has an eight-quality insight — strawberry harvest is a large, labour-dominated cost pool — delivered by a six-quality product, financed on four-quality terms and priced at a three-quality mark. The steps down come from the company's own numbers: coverage 30-50% below the claim, a damage rate that consumes the saving, 110 robots at 31% of the plan, and a preference paying 1.0x to $90M. [S119, S1]

### The recommendation under the downside structures

| Downside structure | Lead recovery at a $25M exit | Recommendation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deck terms: 1x, pari passu, $36.77M stack | 0.59x | Pass; the 1.0x floor is a $39.4-41.6M exit, not $25M | S95 (unverified) |
| 2025 notes carry a senior or 2x preference | 0.21x | Pass; require an equal-rank warranty before any cheque | S95 (unverified) |
| A $10M senior 2028 round ahead of the Series A | 0.31x | Pass; the 2028 round is more likely than not to ask for seniority | S95 (unverified) |
| Pay-to-play in a 2028 down round, lead does not follow | 0.05x | Pass; a cheque with no reserve is a one-shot option | S95 (unverified) |

The recommendation does not change: no downside structure at this mark gives a lead ticket a venture return. The preference stack is one deck sentence and no document; the expected return and this rating assume it ranks equal. It would change on two conditions only: independent quotes at or below the current build cost with a first article built, and a signed renewal at or above the renewal price from outside the chief operating officer's circle. Those would move the unit-economics score, supporting a lead at a lower mark.

### Position sizing

Zero at $72M. The outcomes are 2.2x at 18%, 1.0x at 40% and 0.59x at 42%, an expected 1.04x. On raw multiples Kelly is barely positive, about 15% of a bankroll, because a 1.0x base case scores as no loss; against a 1.5x opportunity cost the excess return is -0.46 per unit, so the check size is zero. Re-entry is two $6M tranches on 200 robots in paid service and two independent v4 quotes at or below $33,000, at a $50-58M pre-money, a 1.5x preference and an equal-rank warranty, with the licence covenant and lender consent as conditions precedent. Maximum loss is $6M before the second tranche; the remaining $6M is reserved for 2028 only if the licence test is met. [S95, S127]

### The next diligence actions

Before a term sheet: obtain the note purchase agreement and seed certificate of designation; commission two manufacturer quotes for the v4 and a firm first-article date; commission an independent cold-storage bruising trial against a named retailer specification; obtain the lender's consent and identify where the cash covenant is tested; obtain counsel opinions on the California equipment standard and Bayh-Dole US-manufacture obligations; run a quality-of-earnings review of the last full year, separating the related-party contract and the grant.

| Rank | Assumption | Base | What would disprove it | Impact on value | Lead MOIC at the adverse outcome | Impact level | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | v4 build cost at 300 units | $33,000, single quote from the noteholder and customer | A second quote above $36,000 | -45% to -60% of equity value: at $44,000 the $16,500 list stops covering depreciation | 0.59x | High | A second quote; a first article slipping past 2027-01 | S1 (unverified) |
| 2 | 2027 price realisation | $12,700 average, some at $16,500 | A renewal at $9,500-10,500 | -25% to -35% of equity value: each $1,000 on 360 robots is $0.36M of revenue; a reversion to $9,500 puts the exit near $40M | 0.96x | High | The first 2027 renewal signature and deposit | S1 (unverified) |
| 3 | Fleet in service by April 2027 | 360 robots | Fewer than 250 delivered by 2027-03 | -20% to -30% of equity value: each 100 robots is $1.27M of revenue and a 250-robot fleet is $3.2M against the $4.6M plan | 1.0x | High | Contracted count below 200 in 2027-02 | S1 (unverified), S95 |
| 4 | Bruising | 3.8% measured; 2.5% assumed | A packer rejecting machine-picked lots | -15% to -20% of equity value: one point of cull is $990 an acre, 36% of the annual fee; a second grower exit holds the exit near $70M | 1.0x | Medium | A second grower exit after the 2026-06 loss | S1 (unverified) |
| 5 | Preference structure and closing date | 1x pari passu; close by 2026-12-15 | A senior or 2x note; a close slipping into Q1 2027 | -45% of the lead's recovery: at a $25M exit the return falls from 0.59x to 0.21x, and a slip breaches the $1.5M covenant near 2027-03-10 | 0.21x | High | Cash below $2.5M; a waiver request | S95 (unverified) |

1. Pass at $72M pre-money: at the $9,500 price growers signed and the single-quoted $48,000 build, one robot-season loses $8,100, and the $12M ticket returns 1.04x on the plan's own probabilities — capital preservation, not a venture return (company-reported inputs). [S1, S95]
2. Re-engage at a $50-58M pre-money with a 1.5x preference and half the cheque staged on two independent v4 quotes at or below $33,000 and 200 robots in paid service, which lifts the same $100M exit from 1.0x to about 1.5x on company-reported terms. [S95]
3. Make the closing conditions substantive: an equal-rank warranty on the preference stack, lender consent, a licence covenant that survives the 2027-12-31 test, and an independent bruising result at or below 2.5%. [S95, S120]
